questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must focus fully on driving. Any other task can be dangerous.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right of way to any emergency vehicle using lights or a siren. Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, pass through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: When can you legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is an available passing lane and the other vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on a road with multiple lanes going the same way. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward ____ of the road.
questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the one ahead. It takes longer to stop when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: What can help you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe following distance.
Drive in the right lane only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe following distance.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without sudden braking, which could cause a crash behind you.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Slow down without hard braking and turn gently back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic when returning to the road.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Signal when slowing down, stopping, or turning. Use your horn when appropriate to let others know you are there.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the speed limit with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down as soon as you see rain, snow, or sleet. These make roads slippery. Safety may require driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not working because of a power outage, what should you do?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you are doing.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop. When it is your turn, go through carefully.

questions.question: If you are in a serious crash, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if you can. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help them. You must report the crash to police if someone is injured, if someone dies, or if there is more than $1,000 in damage (or more than $200 in damage to government property like signs or guardrails).

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is coming toward you. What must you do?

options.text: Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights comes toward you on a one-way street, drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: All three
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol content depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Food slows down alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is always on top and green is always on bottom. On a horizontal signal, red is always on the left and green is always on the right.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with a siren and flashing lights is approaching you. What must you do right away?

options.text: Drive to the right and stop.
Drive to the right and slow down.
Drive to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights, sirens, or warning devices approaches you, drive immediately to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver who does not stop.
One driver who waves others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all vehicles must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection may go first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What color are highway signs that show the distance to the next exit?
questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Signs that show where destinations are located are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on your left at an unmarked intersection where you arrived at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the center line means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves to the right ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves to the right ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road will curve to the right.

questions.question: How much space should you keep between your car and the car ahead of you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: You should keep at least three seconds between your car and the car ahead. In bad weather or at high speeds, keep even more distance.

questions.question: When can you honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your car. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate?

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back.
Ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway. Go to the next exit and turn around safely.

questions.question: What must drivers account for when driving near heavy trucks?

options.text: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.
Heavy trucks need less distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you have a clear view of traffic.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Red means stop. Stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when the driver behind you wants to pass?

options.text: Slow down so the other driver has room to pass easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other driver has room to pass easily.
questions.explanation: Slow down when a driver behind wants to pass. This gives them enough space to pass safely and quickly.

questions.question: What should you expect when driving in areas where children are playing?

options.text: They will know when it is safe to cross.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Children may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking. Slow down and be extra careful in areas where children play.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop until a green light or green arrow appears.
You can turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until a green light or green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop completely. Wait until a green light or green arrow shows before you go.

questions.question: How should you look ahead to prepare for hazards on the road?

options.text: Look at the entire road and both sides.
Rest your left foot on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and both sides.
questions.explanation: Scan the entire road, including both sides. Looking only straight ahead will cause you to miss hazards.
